MPCurve infers latent sample orderings and smooth feature trajectories from
multivariate data. This site presents selected results fitted by
coordinate-ascent variational inference (CAVI) in **MPCurver**. Each study
records the package version used for fitting.
The current simulations and observed-data analyses use MPCurver 0.3.4. Earlier
method fits are retained only as explicitly labeled paired controls.

## Method

MPCurve places samples on an ordered grid and estimates a smooth trajectory
for each feature. With multiple orderings, it also estimates which features
follow each ordering. The [method overview](method.html) explains the model
and algorithm; the [MPCurver package site](https://aguerozz.github.io/MPCurver/)
provides full vignettes and software documentation.

## Simulation

- **Fixed $M=1$**

  - [Simulation summary: three figures](simulation_summary.html) compares four
    methods under shared PCA and Isomap initialization.

  - [One ordering: a noisy spiral](simulation_m1.html) tests recovery of a
    known sample order.
  - [Random B-splines: four methods](simulation_m1_comparison.html) compares
    ordering recovery from common PCA and Isomap starts over 30 replicates at two noise levels,
    with 12 features and a paired extension to 50 features.

- **Fixed $M=2$**

  - [Two orderings: two feature groups](simulation_m2.html) tests recovery of
    feature assignments and both sample orders.

- **Estimate $M$ from the data**

  - [All trajectories monotone](estimate_intrinsic_m.html) is the simpler
    setting. It evaluates automatic-$M$ adaptive EB on 90 fixed datasets with
    three, four, or five true orderings.
  - [One monotone anchor per ordering](estimate_intrinsic_m_smooth.html) is the
    more challenging setting: all other trajectories have smooth peaks and
    troughs. It evaluates the same automatic-$M$ procedure on paired fixed
    datasets.

## Analysis

- [Fitness across environments](fitness.html) compares mutant orderings and
  environment groups, including a fit that uses measurement uncertainty.
- [Pancreatic cell loadings](pancreas.html) compares one- and two-ordering fits
  on the same semi-NMF loading matrix.
